questions.knowledge_point: Solving an Initial Value Problem for a Decoupled Linear System of First-Order ODEs
questions.worked_solution:
We have a decoupled system. Therefore, the general solution is given by

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{3t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Now, we need to find the values of ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}$ using the initial condition $x(0)=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ Substituting $t=0$ into the general solution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x(0) & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}{c}_{1} \\ {c}_{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to our initial value problem is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =-1\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}+1\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{3t} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{3t}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the General Solution to a Decoupled Linear System of Differential Equations
questions.problem:
Find the general solution to the system of differential equations
${\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=-3{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=\pi {x}_{2}(t).\end{aligned}$
questions.worked_solution:
Given a decoupled system of first-order linear ODEs in the form

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 \\ 0 & {\lambda }_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}],
$$

the formula for the general solution is

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{{\lambda }_{1}t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{{\lambda }_{2}t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

First, we write our differential equation in matrix form:

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 \\ 0 & \pi \end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}]
$$

Since the matrix of the differential system is diagonal, the system is decoupled. 

Therefore, the general solution is given by

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{-3t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{\pi t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

questions.problem:
Find the general solution to the system of differential equations
${\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=e{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=-2{x}_{2}(t).\end{aligned}$
questions.worked_solution:
Given a decoupled system of first-order linear ODEs in the form

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 \\ 0 & {\lambda }_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}],
$$

the formula for the general solution is

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{{\lambda }_{1}t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{{\lambda }_{2}t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

First, we write our differential equation in matrix form:

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}e & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}]
$$

Since the matrix of the differential system is diagonal, the system is decoupled. 

Therefore, the general solution is given by

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{et}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-2t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.

questions.problem:
Find the general solution to the system of differential equations
${\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=0 \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(2){x}_{2}(t).\end{aligned}$
questions.worked_solution:
Given a decoupled system of first-order linear ODEs in the form

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 \\ 0 & {\lambda }_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}],
$$

the formula for the general solution is

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{{\lambda }_{1}t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{{\lambda }_{2}t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

First, we write our differential equation in matrix form:

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & \operatorname{ln}⁡(2)\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}]
$$

Since the matrix of the differential system is diagonal, the system is decoupled. 

Therefore, the general solution is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)t} \\  & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{2}^{t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
We have a decoupled system. Therefore, the general solution is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{-\operatorname{ln}⁡2t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{\sqrt{7}t} \\  & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{2}^{-t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{\sqrt{7}t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to find the values of ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}$ using the initial condition $x(0)=[\begin{aligned}9 \\ -5\end{aligned}].$ Substituting $t=0$ into the general solution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x(0) & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}9 \\ -5\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}{c}_{1} \\ {c}_{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to our initial value problem is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =9\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{2}^{-t}+(-5)\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{\sqrt{7}t} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}9 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{2}^{-t}+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -5\end{aligned}]{e}^{\sqrt{7}t}.\end{aligned}
$$
